title: Acalica: Bolivia’s Weather Fairies and Their Limited Sources
metaDescription: Acalica are described in modern references as rarely seen Bolivian weather beings. Here is what that short account says, and what its source trail cannot establish.
description: Acalica are described in modern references as rarely seen Bolivian weather beings. Here is what that short account says, and what its source trail cannot establish.
displayType: Weather beings in modern reference accounts
storyHooks: A village’s weather records disagree with the memory of its oldest resident. Build an original story around that disagreement without presenting it as a recovered Bolivian legend.

sections.origin: The accessible reference trail is short. Wikipedia cites John and Caitlin Matthews’s 2005 Element Encyclopedia of Magical Creatures, page 6. That citation points to a modern compilation; it is not itself a dated field recording.
sections.legend: The brief description associates Acalica with weather, caves, and the appearance of small elderly men. It supplies no full encounter tale with a named narrator, place of collection, or sequence of events.
sections.variants: Without that documentation, this entry does not assign the account to a particular Indigenous community or invent an ancient origin. An English label such as weather fairy is a reference label, not evidence of the original language or category.
sections.culture: This makes a useful example of how to read a bestiary critically: separate the reported traits from a story you create around them. A detailed illustration cannot fill a gap in the written evidence.

sources.title: Wikipedia — Acalica, with its Matthews bibliography

researchNote: The cited encyclopedia page was not independently inspected. The available summary is secondary evidence; this page does not claim a verified oral-history source.

questions.question: What do Acalica look like?
questions.answer: The short modern account describes small elderly men. Details beyond it need a separate source.

questions.question: Is there a documented original Acalica story here?
questions.answer: No. The source available for this page is a brief modern reference summary, and its limits are stated above.
